1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
     9	975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
    10	follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
    11	`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
    12	the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
    13	`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
    14	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
    15	from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
    16	for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    17	replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
    18	`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
    19	nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
    20	scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
    21	corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
    22	matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
    23	edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
    24	Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
    25	a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
    26	`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
    27	cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
    28	every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
    29	same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
    30	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    31	(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
    32	(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
    33	moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
    34	two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
    35	(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

   197	  have hr : 0 < r := inv_pos.2 hsq

   212	  have hnorm := congrArg norm hT

     3	  226|   Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
     4	  227|   nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
     5	  228|   $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
     6	  229|   convention
     7	  230|   \[
     8	  231|     \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
     9	  232|     \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.

    11	  234|   The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function

    27	  803| \begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
    28	  804|   \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
    29	  805|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
    30	  806|   in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
    31	  807|   $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
    32	  808|   \[
    33	  809|     N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
    34	  810|     N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
    35	  811|     N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
    36	  812|     \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
    37	  813|   \]
    38	  814|   Let
    39	  815|   \[
    40	  816|     K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
    41	  817|     \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
    42	  818|   \]
    43	  819|   Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
    44	  820|   $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
    45	  821|   $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
    46	  822|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
    47	  823|     N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
    48	  824|     N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
    49	  825|   \end{equation}
    50	  826|   More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
    51	  827|   $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
    52	  828|   by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
    53	  829|   $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
    54	  830|   and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
    55	  831|   \[
    56	  832|     K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
    57	  833|     \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
    58	  834|   \]
    59	  835|   Then, for every $\theta>0$,
    60	  836|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
    61	  837|     \begin{split}
    62	  838|       0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
    63	  839|       0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
    64	  840|     \end{split}
    65	  841|   \end{equation}
    66	  842|   These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
    67	  843|   domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
    68	  844|   scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
    69	  845|   Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
    70	  846|   give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
    71	  847|   unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.
    72	  848| \end{lemma}
    73	  849| 
    74	  850| \begin{proof}
    75	  851|   Scaling the Fourier representation of $\Gamma$ and using Fourier uniqueness
    76	  852|   gives $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. Radon finiteness and $\alpha > 0$ then imply
    77	  853|   $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$. In particular, $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha V$, where $V = \mu(B_1)
    78	  854|   < \infty$. Therefore, for $a > 0$,
    79	  855|   \[
    80	  856|     \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{a^2+|\xi|^2}
    81	  857|     =\alpha V a^{\alpha-2}
    82	  858|     \int_0^\infty\frac{u^{\alpha-1}}{1+u^2}\ud u<\infty.
    83	  859|   \]
    84	  860|   The last integral is finite since $0 < \alpha < 2$. Substitution into $N_1$
    85	  861|   reduces its finiteness to
    86	  862|   $\int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}(\theta+\lambda)^{\alpha-2} \ud\lambda <
    87	  863|   \infty$: the conditions at zero and infinity are $\alpha_0 > 0$ and
    88	  864|   $\alpha+\alpha_0 < 2$.
    89	  865| 
    90	  866|   For $N_2$ use $|\widehat{G}_s(\xi)| \le \min(s,|\xi|^{-1})$. On $|\xi| \le 1$,
    91	  867|   absolute integration is bounded by
    92	  868|   \[
    93	  869|     V\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
    94	  870|     e^{-\theta(s+t)}|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}st\ud s\ud t<\infty.
    95	  871|   \]
    96	  872|   On $|\xi| > 1$, use $\int_{|\xi|>1}|\xi|^{-2}\mu(\ud\xi) = \alpha
    97	  873|   V/(2-\alpha)$ and the same time integral without $st$. Both time integrals are
    98	  874|   finite by splitting into $s \le t$ and $t \le s$, then using $u = \min(s,t)$
    99	  875|   and $v = |s-t|$; the only singular factor is $v^{-\alpha_0}$, with $\alpha_0 <
   100	  876|   1$. This proves absolute integrability of the displayed spectral formula. For
   101	  877|   each $\xi$, its time integral is nonnegative because the temporal kernel is
   102	  878|   positive definite. Indeed, it is a positive Laplace mixture of the kernels
   103	  879|   $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$. This proves $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$.
   104	  880| 
   105	  881|   The mass identity $G_s(\R^d) = s$ proves the formula for $N_0$. In $N_1$
   106	  882|   change $\lambda = \theta u$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$. In $N_2$ change $s =
   107	  883|   u/\theta$, $t = v/\theta$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$, using
   108	  884|   $\widehat{G}_{u/\theta}(\theta\eta) = \theta^{-1}\widehat{G}_u(\eta)$. These
   109	  885|   changes give exactly the stated powers.
   110	  886| 
   111	  887|   The first tail in~\eqref{E:damped-tail-norms} is a tail of the finite
   112	  888|   nonnegative $N_1(1)$ integral. For the second, $0 \le K_M(r) \le
   113	  889|   |r|^{-\alpha_0}$ and $K_M(r) \to 0$ for $r \ne 0$. The absolute majorant just
   114	  890|   proved permits dominated convergence in $(s,t,\xi)$, giving $N_2^{(M)}(1)^2
   115	  891|   \to 0$. The tail kernel is positive definite by the same Laplace-mixture
   116	  892|   argument, so its quadratic form is nonnegative.
   117	  893| 
   118	  894|   For the multiplier comparisons, define
   119	  895|   \[
   120	  896|     B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   121	  897|     e^{-\theta(s+t)}e^{-\lambda|s-t|}
   122	  898|     \widehat G_s(\xi)\overline{\widehat G_t(\xi)}\ud s\ud t.
   123	  899|   \]
   124	  900|   For each $\lambda>0$ and $\xi$, the positive definiteness of
   125	  901|   $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$ gives $B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)\ge0$.
   126	  902|   The absolute-integrability bound above, $0\le m\le1$ and
   127	  903|   $0\le K_S\le|\cdot|^{-\alpha_0}$ justify changing the integration order:
   128	  904|   \[
   129	  905|     N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2
   130	  906|     =\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   131	  907|     \int_S\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}
   132	  908|     \int m(\xi)B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)\mu(\ud\xi)\ud\lambda.
   133	  909|   \]
   134	  910|   Nonnegativity now proves the second comparison
   135	  911|   in~\eqref{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}. It is used after time integration,
   136	  912|   not pointwise on the oscillating product of wave Fourier kernels. The first
   137	  913|   comparison follows directly from the nonnegative integrand defining $N_1$.
   138	  914|   The choices $S=(0,\infty)$ or $S=(M,\infty)$ give the full or tail bounds.
   139	  915|   Gaussian spatial and Green smoothing contribute products of multipliers in
   140	  916|   $[0,1]$ depending only on $\xi$. Gaussian Green smoothing also preserves
   141	  917|   $G_s(\R^d)=s$, proving its separate assertion for $N_0$. This proves
   142	  918|   Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}.
   143	  919| \end{proof}

   146	 1542| \begin{lemma}[Joint diagram limits and fixed-order construction]
   147	 1543|   \label{L:joint-fixed-order}
   148	 1544|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, every two-chain diagram with $m+n = 2k \ge 2$
   149	 1545|   has a finite joint limit as all its positive vertexwise spatial and temporal
   150	 1546|   widths tend to zero, at arbitrary relative rates. This includes unequal and
   151	 1547|   empty chains. For every $n \ge 1,t > 0,x$, $Y_n^{\boldsymbol a}(t,x)$ has a
   152	 1548|   unique joint $L^2$ limit, denoted $X_n(t,x)$; it is the multiple Stratonovich
   153	 1549|   integral of $g_n$. Green smoothing in dimension three is removed before noise
   154	 1550|   smoothing.
   155	 1551| \end{lemma}

    86	  ascii: "Lean proves, with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, the statements about the Rayleigh supremum E:variational-real-rayleigh: for lambda defined as its square root, a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and I_Psi positive and finite; the operator statements (H_s self-adjoint, form domain H^1, spectral bottom E_s, lambda = sqrt(-E_s)) are not formalized."
    87	  tex: "Lean proves, with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, the statements about the Rayleigh supremum E:variational-real-rayleigh: for $\\lambda$ defined as its square root, a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and $I_\\Psi$ positive and finite; the operator statements ($H_s$ self-adjoint, form domain $H^1$, spectral bottom $E_s$, $\\lambda=\\sqrt{-E_s}$) are not formalized."
    88	- label: T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling
    89	  ascii: "Lean proves, with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for every c > 0: c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 <= U_c for every nonnegative smooth control, S_c^pos <= U_c with the exact C_occ, and U_c = c^m (2 zeta)^(alpha/(2k)) F_0(E_zeta^O) for every zeta > 0, with C_occ and E_zeta^O over the class O modelled by joint representatives; C_2(Gamma,a) <= U_2 is not formalized."
    90	  tex: "Lean proves, with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for every $\\mathfrak{c}>0$: $\\mathfrak{c}I_\\Psi-v_\\Psi/2\\le U_{\\mathfrak{c}}$ for every nonnegative smooth control, $S_{\\mathfrak{c}}^{\\mathrm{pos}}\\le U_{\\mathfrak{c}}$ with the exact $C_{\\rm occ}$, and $U_{\\mathfrak{c}}=\\mathfrak{c}^m(2\\zeta)^{\\alpha/(2k)}F_0(\\mathcal{E}_\\zeta^{\\mathcal{O}})$ for every $\\zeta>0$, with $C_{\\rm occ}$ and $\\mathcal{E}_\\zeta^{\\mathcal{O}}$ over the class $\\mathcal{O}$ modelled by joint representatives; $C_2(\\Gamma,a)\\le U_2$ is not formalized."

  2043	\section{A static phase estimate at first variance order}
  2044	\label{S:static-phase}
  2045	
  2046	A time-block argument would have to carry both position and velocity. We
  2047	establish a uniform estimate for the first variance coefficient with arbitrary
  2048	deterministic initial phase. The covariance may be any member of the original
  2049	three-dimensional class; no endpoint representation is assumed. The estimate
  2050	below is not an all-order propagator bound.
  2051	
  2052	
  2053	
  2054	Let $0 < \alpha < 2$, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonnegative, even, positive-definite
  2055	tempered Radon covariance on $\R^3$, satisfying $\Gamma(rA) =
  2056	r^{3-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$. Its spectral convention is $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
  2057	x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Put
  2058	\begin{equation}\label{E:phase-constants}
  2059	  \begin{split}
  2060	    V&=\mu(B_1),\qquad M=\Gamma(B_1),\qquad
  2061	    R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi V}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\\
  2062	    c_\Gamma&=\frac{(3-\alpha)M}{4\pi},\qquad
  2063	    b_\alpha=2^\alpha+\frac{3^{2-\alpha}}{2-\alpha},\qquad
  2064	    D_\Gamma=c_\Gamma b_\alpha.
  2065	  \end{split}
  2066	\end{equation}
  2067	Here $B_1$ is the open unit ball in the relevant variable. The physical mass $M$
  2068	and the spectral mass $V$ are not identified. Let $p_\epsilon$ be the Brownian
  2069	Gaussian density with covariance $\epsilon I$, and set $\Gamma_\epsilon =
  2070	p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$.
  2071	
  2072	\begin{lemma}[Two static contraction bounds]\label{L:phase-contractions}
  2073	  For $\lambda > 0$, $q \in \R^3$, $a > 0$, and $\epsilon > 0$,
  2074	  \begin{align}
  2075	    \int_{\R^3}\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\lambda^2+|q+\xi|^2}
  2076	    &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},
  2077	    \label{E:phase-resolvent}\\
  2078	    \left|T_\epsilon(a,q)\right|
  2079	    &\le D_\Gamma a^{1-\alpha},
  2080	    \label{E:phase-trace}\\
  2081	    T_\epsilon(a,q)
  2082	    &:=\int_{\R^3}e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)
  2083	    =\int_{\R^3}\widehat{G}_a(q+\xi)e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}
  2084	    \mu(\ud\xi).\nonumber
  2085	  \end{align}
  2086	\end{lemma}
  2087	
  2088	\begin{proof}
  2089	  Homogeneity and Fourier uniqueness give $\mu(B_r) = Vr^\alpha$. In particular,
  2090	  there is no origin atom. For $s > 0$, Schwartz Fourier pairing yields
  2091	  \[
  2092	    \int e^{-s|q+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
  2093	    =\int p_{2s}(x)e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
  2094	    \le\int p_{2s}(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2095	    =\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
  2096	  \]
  2097	  The integrals are finite. Evenness makes the middle integral real, and
  2098	  nonnegativity of $\Gamma$ gives the inequality. Multiply by $e^{-\lambda^2s}$
  2099	  and integrate in $s$. Nonnegative Tonelli on the spectral side gives the
  2100	  resolvent comparison. At $q = 0$ its value is
  2101	  \[
  2102	    \alpha V\int_0^\infty\frac{r^{\alpha-1}}{\lambda^2+r^2}\ud r
  2103	    =R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2}.
  2104	  \]
  2105	  This proves~\eqref{E:phase-resolvent}.
  2106	
  2107	  Since $\mu$ is tempered, its Gaussian weighting is finite. Fourier Fubini
  2108	  therefore gives the identity for $T_\epsilon$. The measure
  2109	  $\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)$ is finite and nonnegative, whence
  2110	  $|T_\epsilon(a,q)| \le T_\epsilon(a,0)$. The radial distribution function of
  2111	  $\Gamma$ is $\Gamma(B_r) = Mr^{3-\alpha}$. Thus, for every nonnegative radial
  2112	  Schwartz function $F$,
  2113	  \[
  2114	    \int F(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2115	    =(3-\alpha)M\int_0^\infty F(r)r^{2-\alpha}\ud r
  2116	    =c_\Gamma\int_{\R^3}F(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\ud x.
  2117	  \]
  2118	  Apply this to $F = G_a*p_{2\epsilon}$, which is radial and Schwartz.
  2119	  Nonnegative Fubini gives
  2120	  \[
  2121	    T_\epsilon(a,0)
  2122	    =c_\Gamma[p_{2\epsilon}*(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})](0)
  2123	    \le c_\Gamma\sup_z(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z).
  2124	  \]
  2125	  Write $r = |z|$. The spherical wave measure has mass $a$, and direct
  2126	  integration over its normal coordinate gives, for $r > 0$,
  2127	  \[
  2128	    (G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z)
  2129	    =\frac{(a+r)^{2-\alpha}-|a-r|^{2-\alpha}}
  2130	    {2r(2-\alpha)}.
  2131	  \]
  2132	  For $r < a/2$, distances from $z$ to the sphere are at least $a/2$, giving the
  2133	  bound $2^\alpha a^{1-\alpha}$. For $r > 2a$, they are at least $a$, giving
  2134	  $a^{1-\alpha}$. On $a/2 \le r \le 2a$, the displayed formula is at most
  2135	  $3^{2-\alpha}a^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$. These bounds also cover the endpoints
  2136	  by continuity and give~\eqref{E:phase-trace}. This proves
  2137	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}.
  2138	\end{proof}
  2139	
  2140	Let $A_\lambda = \lambda^2-\Delta$, and equip deterministic phase pairs with the
  2141	norm
  2142	\begin{equation}\label{E:phase-norm}
  2143	  \|(f,g)\|_\lambda^2
  2144	  =\|f\|_2^2+\|A_\lambda^{-1/2}g\|_2^2.
  2145	\end{equation}

  4689	\subsection{Spectral bounds for $0 < \alpha \le 1$ in all three dimensions}
  4690	
  4691	We now retain Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha
  4692	\le 1$. The covariance is nonnegative and nonnegative definite as in
  4693	Section~\ref{S:model}; when it is a distribution, both these properties and its
  4694	homogeneity are understood distributionally. Let $\mu$ be its positive Radon
  4695	spectral measure in the convention $\gamma(x) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
  4696	x}\mu(\ud\xi)$, and put $V = \mu(\{\xi:|\xi|\le1\})$. No isotropy or spectral
  4697	density is assumed. Write $G_h$ for the positive wave-kernel measure of mass
  4698	$h$, and $G_{h,\eta} = p_\eta*G_h$ for $\eta > 0$; set $G_{h,0} = G_h$. The
  4699	measure notation includes the sphere kernel in dimension three. The mixed-moment
  4700	definition of $A_k(t)$ is now applied to the present $d$-dimensional solution.
  4701	
  4702	\begin{lemma}[Low-$\alpha$ convolution bound]\label{L:low-alpha-convolution}
  4703	  Under the preceding assumptions with $0 < \alpha < 1$, for every $R,h > 0$,
  4704	  \begin{equation}\label{E:low-alpha-radial}
  4705	    \mu(\{\xi:|\xi|\le R\})=VR^\alpha,\qquad
  4706	    \int_{\R^d}\min\{h,|\xi|^{-1}\}\mu(\ud\xi)
  4707	    =\frac{V}{1-\alpha}h^{1-\alpha}.
  4708	  \end{equation}
  4709	  For $\epsilon > 0$ and $\eta \ge 0$,
  4710	  \begin{equation}\label{E:low-alpha-convolution}
  4711	    0\le\int_{\R^d}G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)
  4712	    \le\frac{V}{1-\alpha}h^{1-\alpha},
  4713	    \qquad z\in\R^d.
  4714	  \end{equation}
  4715	  The estimate is uniform in both smoothing parameters and in $z$.
  4716	\end{lemma}
  4717	
  4718	\begin{proof}
  4719	  The spectral measure of $\gamma(c\,\cdot)$ is the pushforward of $\mu$ under
  4720	  $\xi\mapsto c\xi$. Homogeneity and uniqueness of the Fourier transform on
  4721	  tempered distributions therefore give $\mu(A/c) = c^{-\alpha}\mu(A)$ for every
  4722	  Borel set $A$. Equivalently, $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. This proves the
  4723	  ball-mass formula. Since $\mu$ is Radon, $V < \infty$, and continuity from
  4724	  above gives $\mu(\{0\}) = \lim_{R\downarrow0}VR^\alpha = 0$. By the layer-cake
  4725	  identity and Tonelli's theorem,
  4726	  \[
  4727	    \int_{\R^d}\min\{h,|\xi|^{-1}\}\mu(\ud\xi)
  4728	    =\int_0^h\mu(\{\xi:|\xi|\le u^{-1}\})\ud u
  4729	    =V\int_0^h u^{-\alpha}\ud u.
  4730	  \]
  4731	  The endpoint of each indicator has no effect on its $u$ integral. Since
  4732	  $\alpha < 1$, the last expression is the finite quantity
  4733	  in~\eqref{E:low-alpha-radial}. This computation uses ball masses, not a radial
  4734	  density for $\mu$.
  4735	
  4736	  Gaussian weighting gives a finite measure, by the polynomial ball growth of
  4737	  $\mu$. Thus, Fourier Fubini is justified for $\gamma_\epsilon$ and the finite
  4738	  measure $G_{h,\eta}$. From the source's wave-kernel
  4739	  formulas~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(2.3)--(2.5), p.~7},
  4740	  \[
  4741	    \widehat{G}_h(\xi)=\frac{\sin(h|\xi|)}{|\xi|},\qquad
  4742	    G_h(\R^d)=h,
  4743	  \]
  4744	  with value $h$ in the Fourier formula at zero. The Fourier multipliers of
  4745	  $p_\epsilon$ and $p_\eta$ have absolute value at most one, with the latter
  4746	  multiplier equal to one when $\eta = 0$. Consequently,
  4747	  \[
  4748	    \left|\int G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)\right|
  4749	    \le\int_{\R^d}\frac{|\sin(h|\xi|)|}{|\xi|}\mu(\ud\xi)
  4750	    \le\int_{\R^d}\min\{h,|\xi|^{-1}\}\mu(\ud\xi).
  4751	  \]
  4752	  Nonnegativity of $\gamma$ as a distribution implies $\gamma_\epsilon \ge 0$,
  4753	  since Gaussian translates are nonnegative test functions; $G_{h,\eta}$ is also
  4754	  nonnegative. This proves the lower bound in~\eqref{E:low-alpha-convolution}.
  4755	  Combining the preceding displays proves its upper bound. No positivity of the
  4756	  oscillatory Fourier integrand is asserted. This proves
  4757	  Lemma~\ref{L:low-alpha-convolution}.
  4758	\end{proof}

   224	theorem measure_closedBall_eq {μ : Measure (Rd d)} {alpha : ℝ}
   225	    (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha) (R : ℝ) (hR : 0 < R) :
   226	    μ (closedBall 0 R) = ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ alpha) * specV μ := by
   227	  have h := smul_closedBall (E := Rd d) R (0 : Rd d) zero_le_one

   232	`{t ≤ min(h, |ξ|^{-1})} = {|ξ| ≤ t^{-1}}` for `0 < t ≤ h`. -/
   233	theorem levelset_lowKernel {h t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hth : t ≤ h) :
   234	    {ξ : Rd d | t ≤ lowKernel h ξ} = closedBall 0 t⁻¹ := by
   235	  ext ξ
   236	  simp only [mem_ofPred_eq, mem_closedBall_zero_iff, lowKernel]
   237	  split_ifs with hξ
   238	  · simp only [hξ, norm_zero, hth, true_iff]
   239	    exact (inv_pos.2 ht).le
   240	  · have hn : 0 < ‖ξ‖ := norm_pos_iff.2 hξ
   241	    rw [le_min_iff, le_inv_comm₀ ht hn]
   242	    exact ⟨fun h' => h'.2, fun h' => ⟨hth, h'⟩⟩

   247	  ext ξ
   248	  simp only [mem_ofPred_eq, mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_le, lowKernel]
   249	  split_ifs
   250	  · exact hth
   251	  · exact lt_of_le_of_lt (min_le_left _ _) hth

   257	    ∫⁻ t in Ioc 0 h, ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ (-alpha)) =

   262	    ((ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Ioc).2 (Eventually.of_forall fun t ht =>
   263	      Real.rpow_nonneg ht.1.le _)),
   264	    ← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hh, integral_rpow (Or.inl (by linarith)),
   265	    Real.zero_rpow (by linarith)]

   273	theorem integral_lowKernel {μ : Measure (Rd d)} {alpha : ℝ} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
   274	    (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha) (ha1 : alpha < 1) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) :

   276	      ∫ ξ, lowKernel h ξ ∂μ = (specV μ).toReal / (1 - alpha) * h ^ (1 - alpha) := by
   277	  have hV : specV μ < ⊤ := measure_closedBall_lt_top

   330	  have h := spectral_translated_gauss hsp (1 / (2 * ε)) hs x

   355	theorem gammaEps_continuous_bounded {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hμt : IsTempered μ)

   360	    Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ)) * (gaussFactor ε ξ : ℂ) with hF
   361	  have hnorm : ∀ x ξ, ‖F x ξ‖ = gaussFactor ε ξ := by

   363	    simp only [hF, norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,

  2532	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  2533	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2534	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set

     5	variable {C B V : Type} [DecidableEq C]
     6	
     7	def bump (i : C) (d : C → Nat) : C → Nat :=
     8	  fun c => d c + if c = i then 1 else 0
     9	
    10	def counts : List (C × B) → C → Nat
    11	  | [] => fun _ => 0
    12	  | (i, _) :: w => bump i (counts w)
    13	
    14	def raw (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (v₀ : V) : List (C × B) → V
    15	  | [] => v₀
    16	  | (i, b) :: w => F b (J i (raw J F v₀ w))
    17	
    18	def cut (P : V → V) (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V)
    19	    (v₀ : V) : List (C × B) → V
    20	  | [] => v₀
    21	  | (i, b) :: w => F b (P (J i (P (cut P J F v₀ w))))
    22	
    23	theorem raw_support
    24	    (Good : (C → Nat) → V → Prop)
    25	    (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (v₀ : V)
    26	    (hv₀ : Good (fun _ => 0) v₀)
    27	    (hJ : ∀ d i v, Good d v → Good (bump i d) (J i v))
    28	    (hF : ∀ d b v, Good d v → Good d (F b v))
    29	    (w : List (C × B)) : Good (counts w) (raw J F v₀ w) := by
    30	  induction w with
    31	  | nil => exact hv₀
    32	  | cons a w ih =>
    33	    exact hF _ a.2 _ (hJ _ a.1 _ ih)
    34	
    35	theorem cut_eq_raw
    36	    (Good : (C → Nat) → V → Prop)
    37	    (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (P : V → V)
    38	    (v₀ : V) (N : C → Nat)
    39	    (hv₀ : Good (fun _ => 0) v₀)
    40	    (hJ : ∀ d i v, Good d v → Good (bump i d) (J i v))
    41	    (hF : ∀ d b v, Good d v → Good d (F b v))
    42	    (hP : ∀ d v, (∀ c, d c ≤ N c) → Good d v → P v = v)
    43	    (w : List (C × B)) (hN : ∀ c, counts w c ≤ N c) :
    44	    cut P J F v₀ w = raw J F v₀ w := by
    45	  induction w with
    46	  | nil => rfl
    47	  | cons a w ih =>
    48	    have hs : ∀ c, counts w c ≤ N c := by
    49	      intro c
    50	      have hc := hN c
    51	      simp only [counts, bump] at hc
    52	      omega
    53	    have hw := raw_support Good J F v₀ hv₀ hJ hF w
    54	    have hp₀ := hP (counts w) (raw J F v₀ w) hs hw
    55	    have hp₁ := hP (bump a.1 (counts w)) (J a.1 (raw J F v₀ w))
    56	      hN (hJ _ _ _ hw)
    57	    change F a.2 (P (J a.1 (P (cut P J F v₀ w)))) =
    58	      F a.2 (J a.1 (raw J F v₀ w))
    59	    rw [ih hs, hp₀, hp₁]

    23	\begin{lemma}[Full-profile squares in the original space]
    24	  \label{L:occupation-raw-square}
    25	  There is a continuous map $Q:H^1(\R^d;\R) \to H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ with
    26	  \[
    27	    \langle Q(f),Q(h)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    28	    =B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2),\qquad
    29	    \|Q(f)\|^2=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f).
    30	  \]
    31	  For $g \in \mathcal{O}$, the element $\rho_g = J_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}(s\mapsto
    32	  Q(g_s))$ belongs to the original $H_I$ and satisfies
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-raw-identities}
    34	    \|\rho_g\|_{H_I}^2=A(g),\qquad
    35	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}
    36	    =\int_I\int_{\R^d}h_{\Psi,s}(x)g_s(x)^2\ud x\ud s
    37	  \end{equation}
    38	  for every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$. In particular,
    39	  \[
    40	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}\le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g)}.
    41	  \]
    42	\end{lemma}
    43	
    44	\begin{proof}
    45	  Approximate $f$ in $H^1$ by real compact smooth $f_n$.
    46	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} gives
    47	  \[
    48	    \|f_n^2-f_l^2\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}^2
    49	    =C_4(f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l,f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l)
    50	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}N(f_n-f_l)^2N(f_n+f_l)^2\to0.
    51	  \]
    52	  Here $N$ is continuous on $H^1$ and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. Completeness
    53	  defines $Q(f)$; interlacing two approximating sequences proves independence.
    54	  Passing the physical four-linear continuity and Hilbert pairings to limits
    55	  proves the first identities. The same difference bound, first for smooth
    56	  approximants and then by passage to the limit, proves continuity of $Q$.
    57	
    58	  Thus, $F_g(s) = Q(g_s)$ is strongly measurable. Writing $b_s = \|\nabla
    59	  g_s\|_2^2$, the unit norm and $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$ give
    60	  \[
    61	    \int_I\|F_g(s)\|^2\ud s
    62	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}\int_I b_s^{\alpha/2}\ud s
    63	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty .
    64	  \]
    65	  Lemma~\ref{L:positive-raw-embedding} now constructs $\rho_g$ and identifies
    66	  its squared norm with the physical $A(g)$. Joint measurability and
    67	  representative independence follow from the continuous physical pairing on
    68	  $(H^1)^2$. Absolute time integrability follows from the same Schur bound.
    69	
    70	  Choose one compact smooth $\chi$ equal to one on all spatial supports of
    71	  $\Psi_t$. For real $f \in H^1$, smooth approximation gives
    72	  \[
    73	    \langle\Psi_t,Q(f)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    74	    =\lim_n B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f_n^2)
    75	    =C_4(\chi,\Psi_t,f,f)=B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f^2).
    76	  \]
    77	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} justifies these absolute integrals and
    78	  limits. Polarizing~\eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion} gives
    79	  \[
    80	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle
    81	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle\Psi_t,Q(g_s)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    82	    \ud t\ud s .
    83	  \]
    84	  The absolute integrand is bounded by the product of two $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$
    85	  norms against $K$, integrable by Schur and $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. Evenness of
    86	  $\Gamma$ and Tonelli for the nonnegative physical integrands
    87	  yield~\eqref{E:occupation-raw-identities}. Hilbert Cauchy--Schwarz with
    88	  $\|\Psi\|^2 = v_\Psi$ proves the bound. No rough occupation is inserted into a
    89	  stochastic flow. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-raw-square}.
    90	\end{proof}

    92	\begin{proposition}[Original occupation energy and dilation]
    93	  \label{P:raw-occupation-energy}
    94	  With $K_0 = 2^a/(1-a)$,
    95	  \[
    96	    0<C_{\rm occ}\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty .
    97	  \]
    98	  Moreover,
    99	  \begin{align}
   100	    \mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}
   101	    &=D_\zeta C_{\rm occ}^{2/(2-\alpha)},&
   102	    D_\zeta&=\frac{2-\alpha}{2}
   103	    \left(\frac{\alpha}{2\zeta}\right)^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)},
   104	    \label{E:raw-occupation-energy}\\
   105	    C_{\rm occ}
   106	    &=\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}}{2-\alpha}\right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}
   107	    \left(\frac{2\zeta}{\alpha}\right)^{\alpha/2}.
   108	    \label{E:raw-occupation-ratio}
   109	  \end{align}
   110	  In particular, $\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}} > 0$ is finite and equals
   111	  $\zeta^{-\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_1^{\mathcal{O}}$.
   112	\end{proposition}
   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  A unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy: a zero weak gradient makes
   116	  it constant, and an $L^2$ constant on $\R^d$ is zero. Hence, $0 < T(g) <
   117	  \infty$. Spatial covariance Cauchy--Schwarz gives $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   118	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}b_s^{\alpha/4}b_t^{\alpha/4}$. Schur with row bound $K_0$, then
   119	  concavity, proves
   120	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-occupation-bound}
   121	    0\le A(g)\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}.
   122	  \end{equation}
   123	  A fixed compact smooth unit profile, constant in time, belongs to
   124	  $\mathcal{O}$ and has positive $A$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   125	  This proves positivity and finiteness of $C_{\rm occ}$.
   126	
   127	  The map $(U_\ell g)_s(x) = \ell^{d/2}g_s(\ell x)$ is an $H^1$ isomorphism
   128	  preserving unit mass and strong measurability. It has inverse $U_{1/\ell}$ and
   129	  is a bijection on $\mathcal{O}$. The physical Radon change of variables gives
   130	  \[
   131	    A(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A(g),\qquad
   132	    T(U_\ell g)=\ell^2T(g).
   133	  \]
   134	  Indeed, the two densities contribute $\ell^{2d}$, $\ud x$ contributes
   135	  $\ell^{-d}$, and the pushforward of $\Gamma$ contributes $\ell^{\alpha-d}$.
   136	  Approximation extends the identity to full $H^1$. Taking the union over
   137	  $g,\ell$ leaves the class unchanged. For fixed $A,T > 0$, the derivative of
   138	  $A\ell^\alpha-\zeta T\ell^2$ has the sign of $\alpha A-2\zeta
   139	  T\ell^{2-\alpha}$. Its global maximum occurs at $\ell = (\alpha A/(2\zeta
   140	  T))^{1/(2-\alpha)}$ and equals $D_\zeta[A/T^{\alpha/2}]^{2/(2-\alpha)}$. For
   141	  $A = 0$ the supremum is zero as $\ell\downarrow0$. Bounding every ratio by
   142	  $C_{\rm occ}$ gives one inequality in~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-energy}. Fixed
   143	  ratios approaching its positive supremum give the other by continuity of the
   144	  positive power. Algebra gives~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-ratio} and the penalty
   145	  scaling. No optimizer or minimax interchange is assumed. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-occupation-energy}.
   147	\end{proof}

   149	\begin{lemma}[Countable Rayleigh near-occupations]
   150	  \label{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   151	  For fixed $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$
   152	  there is $g_\varepsilon \in \mathcal{O}$ such that
   153	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   154	    I_\Psi^2+T(g_\varepsilon)
   155	    \le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g_\varepsilon)}+\varepsilon .
   156	  \end{equation}
   157	\end{lemma}
   158	
   159	\begin{proof}
   160	  The real $H^1$ space is separable, for example by its isometric embedding
   161	  $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ into a finite product of $L^2$ spaces. Compact smooth
   162	  density therefore supplies a countable real family. Discard zero and normalize
   163	  each member in $L^2$ to obtain $f_j$ dense in the $L^2$-unit $H^1$ class.
   164	  Normalization preserves convergence because the approximating $L^2$ norms tend
   165	  to one. Put $b_j = \|\nabla f_j\|_2^2$ and $R_j(s) = \int
   166	  h_{\Psi,s}f_j^2-b_j$. Bounded-potential form continuity and
   167	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} give $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2 =
   168	  \sup_jR_j(s)$. The canonical functions are measurable, indeed continuous. Let
   169	  $U_j = \{s:R_j(s)>\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2-\varepsilon\}$, $A_1 = U_1$ and $A_j =
   170	  U_j\setminus\bigcup_{i<j}U_i$. These first-index cells are Borel and cover
   171	  $I$. Put $g_\varepsilon(s) = f_j$ on $A_j$. Finite-valued truncations using
   172	  $f_1$ on the remaining cells converge pointwise in $H^1$, proving strong
   173	  measurability. A null-set representative may be filled by $f_1$.
   174	
   175	  With $H_\Psi = \sup_{s,x}h_{\Psi,s}(x) < \infty$, the selection implies
   176	  \[
   177	    b(g_\varepsilon(s))
   178	    <\int h_{\Psi,s}g_\varepsilon(s)^2-\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2+\varepsilon
   179	    \le H_\Psi+\varepsilon .
   180	  \]
   181	  Thus, it belongs to the $\mathcal{O}$. Integrating the near-Rayleigh
   182	  inequality, using Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-raw-square}, gives
   183	  \[
   184	    \int_I\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2\ud s+T(g_\varepsilon)
   185	    \le\langle\Psi,\rho_{g_\varepsilon}\rangle+\varepsilon
   186	    \le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g_\varepsilon)}+\varepsilon .
   187	  \]
   188	  Time Cauchy--Schwarz on the unit interval gives $I_\Psi^2 \le
   189	  \int_I\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2\ud s$. This
   190	  proves~\eqref{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}. No eigenvector, continuum
   191	  selector or limiting occupation is required. This proves
   192	  Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}.
   193	\end{proof}
